Planetary intelligence is the capacity for AI to steer global energy systems within ecological limits, integrating renewables, storage, critical-mineral supply chains, and demand management so that innovation drives resilience and inclusive access.
 
This paradigm calls for digital systems that are distributed, operate within real-world resource constraints, and anticipate long-term impacts on energy security and equity. AI must strengthen the foundations of a just, reliable, and affordable energy transition - rather than increase fragility.
 
Already, AI data centers consume more electricity than 150 individual countries and could demand 6.6 billion m³ of water annually by 2027. The minerals powering this growth - lithium, cobalt, rare earths - are extracted largely from the Global South while most of the value accrues elsewhere. Unless guided by principles aligned with the concept of planetary intelligence, the Energy-AI nexus risks deepening these inequities.
 
The question is no longer whether AI will shape the energy transition - it already is. The real question is how to steer it so that the benefits, resources, and risks are shared fairly.
